
# Challenges encountered and lessons learned {.unnumbered}

## Technical challenges {.unnumbered}

- **Incomplete data.** The data set looked complete at first sight (7,560 movements), but
  counting the movements per combination of factors showed that ID3 and the third
  repetition were missing for some groups. Lesson: always count the observations per cell
  before running an ANOVA, because a mixed ANOVA needs every participant in every cell.
- **Averaging before the ANOVA.** Running the ANOVA on single movements would treat each
  movement as an independent participant and give absurdly small p-values. We had to
  aggregate to one value per participant and condition first (`mt`).
- **A numeric ID.** ID is a factor in the ANOVA but must be a number for the regression.
  We coded it 1 and 2 (`ID_numeric`), which gives slopes per ID step. To compare our
  equations with the article, which uses ID in bits, we had to convert them in the
  discussion (1.7). Lesson: check the units of a model before comparing it with a
  published one.
- **The publication figure.** Combining the participant points, one regression line per
  group and the equations on the same graph required one data frame per layer
  (`mt_regression` for the points and lines, `equation_labels` for the text) and fixed
  axis limits.
- **Included files.** A section file that keeps its own YAML header (`title`, `format`)
  overrides the header of the master document, and the whole report was then rendered in
  HTML under the wrong title. Section files must contain only text and code.

## Individual lessons {.unnumbered}

- **Zoé SAUGE:** I learned to start from the scientific question and break it into precise sub-questions before writing any code, and to choose a suitable library, such as ez, to run the ANOVA reliably. In the discussion, comparing our results with the article taught me to put results on the same scale before comparing them (ID steps vs. bits), and that a simpler method can lead to the same conclusions as long as its limits are clearly stated.
- **Alexis LAGARDE:** Better handling of the method to work with a section folder with a master document where we include all files in it. Working on 1.3 taught me to check the data before testing: counting the cells revealed missing conditions, and averaging per participant avoided pseudo-replication. On the Git side, small commits on one branch per question made teamwork easy, but we should have agreed on branch names and reviewed each other's pull
  requests.
